findings.summary: A terraform test reads only the resources and outputs it names, so no offline check can show that a data source reads a secret; the never-hold rule rests on a reviewer reading the diff.
The instance-role decision record of 2026-11-14 still says the role reads exactly one secret ARN, and the new record extends it without marking it.
The groomed body says the empty-secret read-back prints null, while the CLI's text output prints None; the task file uses None.
Step 6 of the task file asks the maintainer to create a workflow file in a block that holds no single command, which the step format does not cover.

AWS compares the Environment name in the trust case-sensitively while GitHub treats Environment names case-insensitively, so a differently cased name would be refused rather than accepted; this fails closed and is unverified.
The QA reports' Reflection blocks were not posted as comments, because a comment starting with QA: could be read by the close script as a verdict; they are copied into the session summary instead.
